chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:
Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) sent me this will/testament:

"This is what Ali, servant of God, bequeathed and ruled regarding his wealth, seeking the Face of God, that He may admit me thereby to Paradise and divert me thereby from the Fire, and divert the Fire from me: 'On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black'"

That whatever property was in Yanbu' from the property known to be mine in it and what is around it is charity (sadaqah), and its slaves, except Abu Rabbah, Abu Nizar, and Jubayr, are freedmen, upon whom no one has authority, so they are mawla (clients/freemen) who work in the property for five years, and in it is their maintenance, their sustenance, and the sustenance of their families.
And besides that, whatever was mine in Wadi al-Qura, all of it is the property of Banu Fatimah, and its slaves are charity.
And whatever was mine in Dha'ah and its people is charity, except that its slaves are for them like what I wrote for their companions.
And whatever was mine in Udhaynah and its people is charity, and the two poor ones (al-faqirayn), as you know, is charity in the way of God.

And that which I wrote from my properties is a binding, irrevocable charity, whether I am alive or dead; it is spent in every expenditure sought for the Face of God in the way of God and His Face, and for the relatives from Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib, the near and the distant.
And that Hasan ibn Ali will oversee that, eating from it in a good manner and spending it where God wills, in a permissible manner, with no hardship upon him therein.
If he wishes to sell a share of the property to pay off a debt, let him do so if he wishes, with no hardship upon him therein; and if he wishes, let him make it a purchase of ownership.
And that the children of Ali and their mawla (clients) and their properties are under the authority of Hasan ibn Ali.
And if the house of Hasan is not the house of charity, and it seems good to him to sell it, let him sell it if he wishes, with no hardship upon him therein.
And if he sells, then he divides it into three thirds: he makes one third in the way of God, one third for Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib, and the third for the family of Abu Talib.
And he places them where God wills.
And if an event befalls Hasan ibn Ali and Husayn is alive, then it is to Husayn ibn Ali.
And that Husayn will do in it like what I commanded for Hasan; he has like what I wrote for Hasan, and upon him is like what is upon Hasan.
And that which is for Banu Fatimah from the charity of Ali is like what I made for the children of Ali.

And I only made what I made for the two sons of Fatimah seeking the Face of God and honoring the sanctity of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), glorifying it and dignifying it, and his pleasure with them.
And if an event befalls Hasan and Husayn, then the last of them looks into the children of Ali.
If he finds in them someone he is pleased with in his guidance, his Islam, and his trustworthiness, then he makes it to him if he wishes.
And if he does not find in them some of what he wants, then it is in the children of the two sons of Fatimah.
If he finds in them someone he is pleased with in his guidance, his Islam, and his trustworthiness, then he makes it to him if he wishes.
And if he does not find in them some of what he wants, then he makes it to a man from the family of Abu Talib whom he is pleased with.
If he finds that the elders and those of opinion among the family of Abu Talib have passed away, then he makes it to a man he is pleased with from Banu Hashim.

And he stipulated upon the one to whom he entrusts it that he leaves the property upon its foundations and spends the fruits where he commands him from the way of God and its aspects, and the relatives from Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib, the near and the distant.
Nothing from it is sold, nor is it given as a gift, nor is it inherited.
And the property of Muhammad ibn Ali is a side portion, and it is to the two sons of Fatimah.
And that my slaves who are in the small sheet that I wrote are freedmen.
This is what Ali ibn Abi Talib ruled regarding his properties; this, the day after he arrived at his residence, seeking the Face of God and the Last Home.
"And God is the one sought for help" in every state.
And it is not permissible for a Muslim man who believes in God and the Last Day to change anything of what I bequeathed in my property, nor to contradict my command in it, whether near or distant.

As for after this, then my nursing maidservants, upon whom I revolve, are seventeen; among them are mothers of living children with them their children, and among them are pregnant, and among them is one who has no child.
My ruling regarding them, if an event befalls me, is that whoever of them has no child and is not pregnant, she is freed for the Face of God, upon whom no one has authority.
And whoever of them has a child and is pregnant, she is kept for her child, and she is from his share (of Umm al-Walad).
If her child dies while she is alive, then she is freed, upon whom no one has authority.

This is what Ali ruled regarding his property, the day after he arrived at his residence. Witnessed by Abu Shimr ibn Abrahah, and Sa'sa'ah ibn Suhan, and Sa'id ibn Qays, and Hayyaj ibn Abi al-Hayyaj. And Ali ibn Abi Talib wrote it with his own hand.
"To the ten days remaining of Jumada al-Ula, the year thirty-seven."

key_terms.اَلدَّارُ: House/Residence - referring to the property or estate.
key_terms.اَلصَّحِيفَةُ: The sheet/document - the written record of the will.
key_terms.اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Hasan ibn Ali - the primary overseer of the charitable estate.
key_terms.اَلْوَلِيدَةُ: Nursing maidservant (Umm al-Walad) - a slave who bears her master's child.
key_terms.رَقِيقٌ: Slaves - specifically those attached to the property.
key_terms.صَدَقَةٌ: Charity (Sadaqah) - property dedicated for charitable purposes, inalienable.
key_terms.عَتِيقٌ: Freedman - a slave who has been freed.
key_terms.مَوَالٍ: Mawla (clients/freemen) - those under the patronage of the property or family.

ai.seo_question: What are the specific provisions of Ali ibn Abi Talib's will regarding his properties and succession of management?
ai.summary: This foundational will (wasiyyah) of Imam Ali (AS) serves as a critical precedent in Shia jurisprudence for the concept of *waqf* (endowment), establishing that his properties in regions like Yanbu' and Dha'ah were dedicated permanently to God and the Ahl al-Bayt, rendering them inalienable and non-inheritable. The text outlines a sophisticated succession plan where Hasan, then Husayn, and subsequently the descendants of Fatima or Ali manage these assets, emphasizing their role as trustees rather than absolute owners. This document underscores the theological significance of preserving the wealth of the Prophet's household for charitable and religious purposes, reflecting the Shia view of their unique spiritual and material stewardship.
